entries.title: Who the folk are
entries.answer: Each folk is its own person: a name, two traits, a pastime, likes and dislikes, a dream, a mood, and its own opinion of you. Right-click one to meet it.
more: Each folk is its own person: a name, two traits (hardworking, easygoing, sociable, shy, cheerful, grumpy, generous or curious), a pastime, a quirk, a favourite food, something it loves and something it can't abide, a dream, a mood, memories, and a separate opinion of each player.
steps: Right-click a folk to talk and see its trade, nature and how it feels.
Open its Profile from the talk screen for everything about it.
tips: A grump is short with you, a shy folk stumbles over words, a cheerful one can't help an exclamation mark.
Folk never write in chat: what they say shows in a speech bubble over their head.

entries.title: Making friends with the folk
q: how do i make friends with the villagers
how to get villagers to like me
how do i make the folk like me
how do i get on with the folk
how to be liked in the village
how do i become friends with a villager
how to get reputation with villagers
entries.answer: Talk to each folk once a day and give presents it likes. Help it with errands and quests, and keep monsters off it.
more: Folk warm to you one at a time.
When the folk who know you think well enough of you on average, you're a Friend of {town}.
steps: Talk to a folk every day: the first word each day warms it (+2; +3 for a sociable folk, +1 for a shy or grumpy one).
Give presents (Trade → Give, holding the item): a thing it loves +15, its favourite food +12, what its trade needs +8, food or useful things +5. Up to three a day count.
Say 'Well done!' (Chat tab) once a day: +3.
Ask it to come with you, eat together, help with its errands ('Can I help?') and take its quests.
Kill monsters near folk: everyone who saw thinks better of you, and saving one that cried for help is never forgotten.
controls: Ask → Can I help? · Any work?
tips: Ask 'About you' to learn its favourite food and what it loves; the Profile's About tab lists both.
Carrying the Medal or Key of the Town makes the folk warm to you faster each day.
Folk talk about you to each other: a good name spreads ahead of you.
warn: Hitting a folk costs a lot (and everyone who saw it thinks less of you).
A present it hates, or rotten flesh, makes it think worse of you.

entries.title: Your standing in a town
q: what does friend of the village mean
how do i become an honoured guest
how do i become a hero of the village
how do i check my reputation
what does the town think of me
entries.answer: Your standing is what the folk who know you think of you on average, from Outcast to Hero. Press U to see it.
more: Your standing is the average warmth of the folk who know you: Outcast, Unwelcome, Stranger or Visitor, Friend of the village (average 12+), Honoured guest (30+, known by 3+), Hero (50+, known by 5+).
The U page shows it as a bar, and any folk will tell you ('My standing').
steps: Or ask a folk: Town → My standing; it names who thinks the world of you and who doesn't trust you.
tips: Honoured guest: the town resolves to build you a house of your own and hands you its key.
Hero: a night in your honour, the town's medal, and a statue of you on the square.
Your best title anywhere is shown in gold after your name.
warn: As an outcast nobody will talk to you; only a present, or paying what you owe, is heard.

entries.title: Giving presents
q: how do i give a gift to a villager
what should i give the folk
what do villagers want as gifts
entries.answer: Hold the present and choose Trade, then Give, on the talk screen. Things it loves count the most.
more: What each folk loves is one of: flowers, something sweet, a gem, a book, music, fish, a good tool, wool or gold.
Up to three a day count.
steps: Find out what it loves: ask 'About you', or open its Profile → About.
Give up to three presents a day: more than that doesn't count.
tips: A loved thing that isn't food is kept as its own and moves house with it.
Spectacles delight an old folk who has none.
On its birthday a present means more (the talk screen suggests it).
warn: It refuses what it hates, and thinks the worse of you for offering. Spider eyes and rotten flesh are never welcome by most.

entries.title: Folk moods and needs
q: how do i make folk happy
folk needs food rest company comfort
entries.answer: A folk's mood comes from its own life: its bed, food, friends, rest and how the town is doing. Ask it 'How are you?' to hear why.
more: A folk's mood comes from its own life: up for its own bed, food, a partner, friends, a present, its pastime, a day of rest and a thriving town; down for hunger, sleeping rough, loneliness, being hit, grief or a miserable town.
Its four needs are Food, Rest, Company and Comfort, shown as bars on its profile.
steps: Ask 'How are you?' (Chat tab): it says its mood and why.
Open its Profile for the four needs as bars.
Check the town's contentment on the town's books Overview.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → How are you?
tips: A happy folk works a little quicker, a miserable one slower.
Town contentment (out of 100) adds up food, homes, mood, safety, things to enjoy, wages and rest: 80+ thriving, under 25 miserable.
warn: After three miserable days, somebody leaves the town.

entries.title: A folk's profile
q: how do i see a villager's details
how do i see what a folk thinks of me
where can i see a folk's family
how do i check a folk's job and level
what businesses does this folk own
how do i see a folk's business
entries.answer: A folk's profile shows everything about it in seven tabs, its businesses among them. Press Profile at the top of its talk screen.
more: A folk's profile shows it as a person: its model, name, age, trade and level, mood and four needs, and seven tabs: Overview (traits, quirk, dream, likes), Work (trade, what it is doing now and why, knacks, wage, kit), Business (every business it owns or works in: where, its role, this week's takings and profit, the till, its hands, how long open, growing or struggling, and its plans; click one for its books), Family (family, home, friends), Town (citizen or visitor, offices, what it thinks of you and how to raise it, and its recent life), Day (today's plan and memories) and Things (pack, purse, home comforts).
steps: Right-click the folk and press Profile at the top of the talk screen.
Or click its name anywhere it's a link (the town's books, a card), or a row on the Folk page.
controls: Town's books → People → Folk → click a row
tips: Esc goes back to the screen you came from.
Keys 1 to 7 switch tabs.
A business's books open from the Business tab when the town's books would show them to you.
In creative, a folk's name offers Teleport to when it has wandered off.

entries.title: Skills, knacks and a folk's work record
q: how to see a folk's career
entries.answer: Folk level up in their trade as they work and pick knacks for themselves. The talk screen's Skills page shows them.
more: Each also picks knacks for itself (trade, nature and purse perks), shown as pips on the talk screen's Skills page.
'Full profile' and the pack's Work done button show its whole record: blocks mined, trees felled, crops grown, fish caught, things made and built.
steps: Talk → Skills: its knacks.
Talk → Full profile (or its pack → Work done): its record.
Ask 'Good at?' (About → Work & pay) to hear it in its own words.

entries.title: Favourite folk (following a folk)
q: how do i follow a folk
how do i track a villager
how do i keep an eye on one folk
entries.answer: Favourites are folk you follow: you see how they get on and hear news of them. Click the star on a folk's profile.
more: Star a folk on its profile to add it to your favourites: a shortlist of cards showing each one's level, mood, worth and what it's doing, with charts of its progress and a timeline of its life.
steps: Open a folk's profile and click its star (or Follow the elder on the welcome card).
Open the list: the favourites key (unbound until you set it in Controls), the star in the town's books header, or from a profile.
Click a card for its Progress, Life and Details tabs; pin one to the on-screen tracker.
controls: Favourites key (set it in Options → Controls)
tips: Toasts and the tracker can be turned off in the client config (mc_assistant-ui-client.toml).

entries.title: Saying sorry and mending things
q: how do i apologise to a villager
i hit a villager by accident
villagers hate me what do i do
how do i stop being an outcast
entries.answer: Say 'I'm sorry' on the talk screen (Chat, then More chat). Each folk accepts one apology a day, and grudges fade by themselves.
more: A folk accepts one apology a day, and it mends a little of what a hit broke.
Grudges also fade by themselves every day: quickly for an easygoing or generous folk, slowly for a grumpy one.
steps: Talk → Chat → More chat → I'm sorry (the talk screen suggests it when you're out of favour).
Give a present it likes.
Pay any fine you owe (Town → The watch → Pay a fine).
Or stay away a while and let it cool.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → I'm sorry
warn: Once the town has made you an outcast, only a gift or paying what you owe is heard.

entries.title: What the town gives its friends
q: what do i get for being a hero
will the village build me a house
statue of me in the village
why did a villager give me something
entries.answer: Friends of the town are rewarded: presents and keepsakes from fond folk, a house as an Honoured guest, and a feast, medal and statue as a Hero.
more: A folk fond of you sometimes gives you something of its own as you pass.
A close friend gives you a named keepsake once, and writes to you weekly.
tips: Finishing a quest story earns the Medal of the Town; two stories or ten quests (as a friend) earn the Key to the Town and the title Freeman.

entries.title: Protecting the folk
q: a villager is shouting for help
save a villager from a zombie
do folk thank me for killing monsters
entries.answer: A folk attacked by a monster shouts for help. Kill the monster and it, its family and friends never forget it.
more: Kill the monster and you saved its life: it never forgets, its friends and family think better of you, and the chronicle records the rescue.
Any monster you kill near folk wins you thanks from everyone who saw.

entries.title: Emotes: wave, bow, shake hands
q: how do i wave at a villager
entries.answer: Hold V for the emote wheel, point at an emote and let go. You can also wave, bow or shake hands from a folk's talk screen.
more: A handshake goes to the folk you're looking at.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Chat → More chat → Wave · Shake hands · Bow
tips: In a small window the wheel lays its emotes out in two columns instead of a ring.

entries.title: The elder
entries.answer: The elder is the town's leader, elected every ten days. It sets the food reserve and wages and gives orders that move hands between trades.
more: The elder is the town's leader (the reeve, thane or mayor, as the land calls it): chosen by election every ten days.
Fill the larder, Dig deep, Man the walls) that moves a few hands between trades.
steps: Ask any folk 'Elder's orders' (Ask → Favours) to hear the current order.
Tell the elder what it should order ('we need more miners'): if it thinks well of you, it agrees.
controls: [Right-click] a folk → Ask → Favours → Elder's orders
